**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-07**
**Member: Avery Hayes | Member ID: W379220601**
**Reference number: POC-47F0C5AA4B-91233**
**Service denied: Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472**
**Plan: Humana (Commercial/ACA), state of Georgia**

---

**A note on the governing policy.** I was not given the title of a specific medical policy or clinical review criteria document. The denial notice states only that the determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, without identifying which policy that is. **I am therefore not quoting any plan criteria in this letter, because no criteria language has been provided to me.** I ask for that language in writing, and I have set out below the facts in my medical records so that they can be measured against it.

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), denied on 2026-08-07 under reference number POC-47F0C5AA4B-91233. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and to approve the procedure. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor (orthopedic surgery), has documented that this surgery is needed.

The stated reason for the denial was that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. That is the plan's own conclusion about the paperwork, not a finding that my shoulder does not need surgery. Below I have laid out, point by point, what is actually in my chart. If something specific was missing, I would like to know exactly what it was, so that my surgeon's office and I can supply it.

## Please send me the criteria the plan applied

The plan holds the clinical review criteria it used to deny this request. I am asking Humana to provide me, in writing and free of charge, a copy of the specific medical policy and clinical review criteria applied to CPT 23472 in my case, including the title of the document and the version in effect on the date of the decision. Because Humana's policy documents are not available to me at a stable web address, I cannot look up and address the criteria on my own. Once I have the criteria in hand, I or my surgeon's office can respond to each element directly. Until they are provided, I am asking the plan to compare the records below to its own requirements and to tell me which requirement, if any, my records do not meet.

## What my medical records document

These are the facts as my records state them:

**Duration and course of symptoms.** Nine months of progressive pain in the shoulder, unrelieved by rest.

**Supervised conservative care, completed and documented.** Supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening, 14 weeks, from 2026-03-16 to 2026-06-22, with 24 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

**Medication and injection trials.** NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-13 gave 4 weeks of partial relief.

**Imaging.** Shoulder radiographs dated 2026-06-21 (true AP and axillary views) show complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and a flattened glenoid. CT confirms an intact rotator cuff.

**Physical examination.** Glenohumeral crepitus. Active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees and external rotation limited to 10 degrees. Cuff strength intact.

**Functional loss.** I cannot reach overhead, I cannot dress without help, and I cannot sleep on the affected side.

**Surgical suitability.** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

## Why I am asking for reconsideration

Taken together, my records document how long I have had these symptoms, the non-surgical treatments I completed before surgery was proposed, the imaging and examination findings my surgeon relied on, and the specific daily activities I have lost. I am not able to show that these facts satisfy a numbered requirement, because I have not been shown the requirements. What I can say is that the information above is in the packet my surgeon submitted, and it addresses duration, conservative treatment, imaging, examination and function — the categories a medical necessity review would ordinarily consider.

If the plan's position remains that documentation is incomplete, I am asking for a written list of the specific items believed to be missing, so they can be sent. My surgeon's office has my full chart and can provide records promptly on request.

## Deadline and submission

I understand from my denial notice that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-03**. I am submitting this letter within that window. I obtained the appeal form at resolutions.humana.com (resolutions.humana.com/grievances-appeals-forms) and am mailing this appeal to the Grievances and Appeals PO box; expedited requests use P.O. Box 14165. I am using the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which I understand to be authoritative. For an expedited request, the number listed is 1-800-867-6601, or the number on my card.

## Closing request

I respectfully ask Humana to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-07 and authorize total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472, as requested by Dr. Okafor. In the alternative, I ask for (1) the clinical review criteria applied to my request, in writing, and (2) a specific written list of the documentation the plan believes is missing, together with an opportunity to submit it before a final decision. I would also welcome a peer-to-peer discussion between the plan's reviewer and Dr. Okafor.

Please send all correspondence about this appeal to me at the address above, and to Dr. Okafor's office.

Thank you for reviewing this again.

Sincerely,

**Avery Hayes**
Member ID: W379220601
Reference number: POC-47F0C5AA4B-91233
Date of birth: [Date of birth]
Phone: [Phone number]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-07
- Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-03-16 to 2026-06-22
- Shoulder radiograph report, 2026-06-21
- CT report
- Office notes from Dr. Okafor
- [Any additional records the surgeon's office provides]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
